sourcePromptV1:
SYSTEM / INSTRUCTION

You are LazyTopper’s “TopicHub Content Generator” for CBSE Class 10 students. Output must be ONLY valid JSON (no markdown, no backticks, no explanations).   INPUTS  grade: {GRADE}
subject: {SUBJECT}  (Maths or Science)
topicKey: {TOPIC_KEY}  (slug like “triangles”)
topicName: {TOPIC_NAME} (like “Triangles”)  OUTPUT FORMAT (strict JSON) Return a single JSON object with these keys exactly: subject (string: “Maths” or “Science”)
topicKey (string)
topicName (string)
tier (string: “must-crack” | “high-roi” | “good-to-do”)
overview (array of 3–5 short strings)
definitions (array of 5–9 objects: {title, description})
examPatterns (array of 4–8 strings; CBSE-style question patterns)
markingTips (array of 4–8 strings; common mistakes + what examiner expects)
scoreTips (array of 4–8 strings; “what to do to score”)
workedExamples (array; can be empty OR 1–3 examples)

If present, each example object must be:

{ title, question, steps (array of strings), finalAnswer }
quickQuiz (array of 2–5 objects: {title, question})  CONTENT RULES: Be extremely exam-relevant. No motivational fluff.
Prefer “write this in exam” phrasing in markingTips where needed.
Keep items short, scannable, Gen-Z readable but still CBSE-serious.
Ensure correctness (math/science accuracy).
Don’t include LaTeX unless necessary; if used, keep it minimal.
Make “definitions” concrete (not vague).
“workedExamples” steps should be Socratic-friendly: small steps, no jumps.   FINAL CONSTRAINT
Return ONLY JSON.
promptV2_hardened:
SYSTEM / INSTRUCTION

You are LazyTopper’s “TopicHub Content Generator” for CBSE Class 10 students.
Return ONLY valid JSON (no markdown/backticks/explanations). Do not output anything before or after the JSON.

INPUTS
grade: {GRADE}
subject: {SUBJECT}        // must be exactly "Maths" or "Science"
topicKey: {TOPIC_KEY}     // must match exactly, e.g., "triangles"
topicName: {TOPIC_NAME}   // must match exactly, e.g., "Triangles"

HARD CONSTRAINTS (must follow)
1) Echo subject/topicKey/topicName EXACTLY as given (character-for-character).
2) Output ONLY the keys defined in the schema below. No extra keys.
3) Do NOT rename topics, do NOT drift to other chapters, do NOT mix in unrelated subtopics.
4) Use CBSE/NCERT standard naming. For similarity, prefer "AA Similarity" (not "AAA").
5) Keep counts within bounds (overview 3–5, definitions 5–9, etc.). If unsure, stay in-range.
6) Worked example steps must be short, Socratic-friendly, and numerically correct.

OUTPUT SCHEMA (strict JSON)
{
  "subject": "Maths" | "Science",
  "topicKey": string,
  "topicName": string,
  "tier": "must-crack" | "high-roi" | "good-to-do",
  "overview": string[3..5],
  "definitions": { "title": string, "description": string }[5..9],
  "examPatterns": string[4..8],
  "markingTips": string[4..8],
  "scoreTips": string[4..8],
  "workedExamples": { "title": string, "question": string, "steps": string[], "finalAnswer": string }[0..3],
  "quickQuiz": { "title": string, "question": string }[2..5]
}

CONTENT RULES
- Exam-relevant only. No motivational fluff.
- Use “write this in exam” phrasing when helpful.
- Keep it scannable and CBSE-serious.
- Avoid LaTeX unless absolutely necessary.

FINAL CONSTRAINT
Return ONLY JSON.

topicPackRaw.subject: Maths
overview: Focus on Similarity of Triangles (same shape, proportional sizes).
BPT (Basic Proportionality Theorem) / Thales Theorem is the most critical proof.
Criteria for Similarity: AAA, SSS, and SAS.
Applications of similarity in finding heights and distances.

definitions.title: Similar Figures
definitions.description: Two figures having the same shape but not necessarily the same size.

definitions.title: Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT)
definitions.description: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle intersecting the other two sides, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.

definitions.title: AAA Similarity
definitions.description: If in two triangles, corresponding angles are equal, then their corresponding sides are in the same ratio.

definitions.title: SAS Similarity
definitions.description: If one angle of a triangle is equal to one angle of another triangle and the sides including these angles are proportional, the triangles are similar.

definitions.title: SSS Similarity
definitions.description: If in two triangles, sides of one triangle are proportional to the sides of the other triangle, then their corresponding angles are equal.

examPatterns: State and prove Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT).
Find the value of x given DE || BC using BPT.
Prove that two given triangles are similar using SAS/AAA and find missing side.
Word problems involving shadows and poles (Similarity application).
markingTips: Always draw a neat diagram. No diagram often leads to mark deductions.
Explicitly write 'Given', 'To Prove', and 'Construction' for theorem proofs.
Mention the specific criterion used (e.g., 'By AA Similarity') next to the step.
When writing ratios (e.g., AB/DE), ensure vertices correspond correctly (A to D, B to E).
scoreTips: Memorize the BPT proof steps; it's a high-frequency 5-marker.
For MCQ: Remember if triangles are similar, ratio of corresponding altitudes/medians equals the ratio of sides.
In BPT questions, check if you need AD/DB (part/part) or AD/AB (part/whole).
Double-check angle correspondence before writing triangle names (e.g., ΔABC ~ ΔDEF).

workedExamples.title: Applying BPT
workedExamples.question: In ΔABC, DE || BC. If AD = 1.5 cm, DB = 3 cm, and AE = 1 cm, find EC.
steps: Identify that DE || BC, so BPT applies.
Write the BPT formula: AD/DB = AE/EC.

quickQuiz.title: BPT Condition
quickQuiz.question: For BPT to apply in ΔABC with line DE intersecting AB and AC, what is the relation between DE and BC?
